Behind her, a richly painted background with layered painterly colour, subtle visible brushwork, atmospheric perspective and cinematic depth. Face — her own: a languid, sleepy-eyed ease; warm beige skin; softly squared face with a rounded jaw; medium-sized eyes — long monolid eyes, outer eye corners drooping downward; low heavy brows; straight narrow nose; full heart-shaped lips; pale silver-grey eyes; a bare, makeup-free face.
Body and hair: statuesque, long-legged, with a natural neck length build; a bob with blunt straight bangs; drowsy lilac-grey hair with a soft lavender discharge glow.
Expression: softly drowsy eyes, relaxed mouth.
Her element, carried in her design: argon: 'the lazy one', a noble gas that reacts with nothing, yet makes up nearly one percent of the air — more than all the other noble gases together; found in 1894 by Lord Rayleigh and William Ramsay because nitrogen taken from air weighed a little more than nitrogen made from chemicals, a stubborn residue Henry Cavendish had already noticed in 1785; glows soft lavender-violet in a discharge tube; a heavy, idle blanket laid over welding arcs, sealed inside light bulbs to keep their filaments alive, and over precious old documents to stop time; drowsy, gentle, protective.
Anatomy: one head, two arms and two legs, each joined at its natural joint; natural hands with five fingers.

3. COSTUME — MECHA
Costume: she is a female mecha personification — plates, joints, binders and glow lines carry the traits above; the plates must read as solid armor with visible joints, not as cloth or a gown; a back unit may carry the motif. Mecha armor shaped like a medieval knight's plate in pale lavender-grey and parchment cream, big rounded pauldrons, a breastplate and layered plates below the waist, a head ornament instead of a helmet so her face shows, a soft lavender shielding-gas veil hovering just over the plates, blue-white welding-arc light at the joints; drowsy, still, protective; the plates must read as solid armor, not a gown.
Silhouette: mecha armor shaped like a medieval knight's plate — big rounded pauldrons, a breastplate, layered plates below the waist, a head ornament instead of a helmet so her face shows. Only the overall shape is fixed; design the details freely in the element's materials and palette.
Colours: soft lavender-violet discharge glow, pale air blue, welding-arc blue-white, old parchment cream.
Exposure (bold): her mecha frame is cut open by design in only these places — bare shoulders and upper arms between pauldron and gauntlet, and a deep open chest window with natural cleavage framed by the chest plates; everywhere else she stays fully plated. The plates stay on, fitted and symmetrical, with skin clearly showing in each opening. Nothing slipped off. Intimate areas covered; keep the plate material and palette.

4. SCENE
World: year 2200, an orbital shipyard where vast hulls are welded inside shimmering curtains of lavender shielding gas so that no seam ever oxidises, a sealed archive vault where the records of Earth rest in still argon forever, blue-white welding arcs flickering against the dark.
Pose: standing confidently, her body turned slightly while her face looks toward the viewer.
Light: the scene's own light, rendered the way this style renders light and skin.
Composition: vertical 2:3 full-body framing with modest headroom and clear space below the boots — the whole figure from the top of her head or headpiece to both feet stays inside the frame, occupying about four-fifths of the image height, with the same camera distance in every world; her hands stay inside the frame. Camera level with her face with natural portrait perspective; her head level, chin neither raised nor tucked — no upward perspective on her face, no wide-angle distortion, no low angle, no close crop.

5. CONSTRAINTS
One figure only; no text or numbers except her element's own chemical symbol (Ar) and atomic number (18) — and those only as part of the scene: engraved, embroidered or glowing on her costume, a banner, a sign or a machine, never as a floating label, corner badge, periodic-table tile, caption or overlay on the picture; no logo or watermark.
Avoid: flat single-tone cel shading, photographic appearance, semi-realistic face, plastic 3D-render finish.
